The canonical Source owner constructs its real read-only/mutable owners, initializes the Source security-cookie owner, verifies pages/relationships, and publishes only after the parent ACK. It remains alive through CRT teardown.
Normal startup constructs GameSingletonHost and initializes observer dispatch, then constructs GameVfsHost with verified data and invokes phase2.
GameVfsHost owns an actual GameNativeVfsApplication. phase2 calls its initialize_core once before mounts/package scans. The application remains private and no wrapper exposes the new opt-in.

Real resource/stream types and physical-pool process initialize; singleton_lifetime_allocate obtains the genuine A0 allocation. Runtime construction binds current services, core construction/registration completes, the resource-registry deletion domain binds, then the completion flag is set.

The retained runtime owns the concrete path, archive, physical, finite-dispatch and deletion contexts. register_core constructs the derived manager on that A0 allocation, publishes it through the application-owned cell, installs the original identities, and registers FileStore and MPKG after physical.
Normal shutdown drains singletons while VFS and all its services still exist. GameVfsHost is deleted afterward.

shutdown drains the actual registered singleton manager, retires the attached VFS runtime, frees/clears the singleton manager, and keeps publication cells alive throughout. The runtime clears its matching VFS publication and rejects later publication through the retired guard.

steps.action: Run one fresh rebuilt Win32 child through the existing parent/reservation/CanonicalCrtV2 path. Keep the real log, canonical data owner and code image. Instantiate the concrete host/application, initialize the core once, and retain both owners until the shared drain completes. Record the actual physical-pool registration result and any genuine diagnostics.

Borrow application.runtime(), application.owners(), and application.borrow_raw_services(). Require one identical live pointer across runtime.actual_manager(), the existing owner publication and the service publication. Observe its current profile D68D04, +90=00530620, +8C=00735B30 and real three-factory core list. Observe that the same actual singleton-manager registration vector contains that A0 owner; do not manufacture or register another record.

Snapshot all A0 bytes and the actual singleton-manager active registration records into read-only comparison buffers. These buffers are never used as managers and are never written back. Call the real borrowed services.bindings.open_failure_entry with the captured Original +90 identity and real manager, then require the snapshots/publications unchanged. This covers the existing typed-no-op branch without executing a numeric identity.

Qualify the trusted linked raw C3 and notifier from exact named Source symbols and the freshly built image. Call application.publish_and_borrow_raw_failure_manager(); require the identical returned A0 and the exact trusted raw C3 address at +90. Compare all A0 bytes: only the four bytes at +90 may differ; preserve +8C, +18, both existing publications and all registration records.

Call the same application method a second time. Require the same pointer and exact whole-record/publication/registration equality with the first published result. This is one idempotent mode transition on the same owner, not a second owner fixture.

Use the same retained runtime bindings to call open_failure_entry with the actual published +90 word and real manager. Require unchanged records. Then call the exact declared raw_notify_native_vfs_request_failure_00bd9e30(real_manager, forwarded_edx, discarded_word) once, using two independently recorded distinct scalar DWORD witnesses, not an inferred equality or +18 load. Require return and unchanged full A0/registration/publication snapshots. Do not inject or call an arbitrary target, mount anything, invoke Original code, or call BF5030.

End all borrowed uses before host.shutdown begins. Keep application/runtime/data/services/code alive during that actual shared drain. After it returns, inspect only still-live publication cells: VFS and singleton-manager publications must be null. Never inspect the freed A0 or old registration vector. A fresh application API request must throw at the retired-runtime guard before any owner dereference. Then destroy the already-drained application and host, and allow the genuine process/physical-pool CRT teardown on normal success.

one_focused_future_case.failure_lifetime: Catch initialization or drain failures while both actual heap-owned C++ objects and canonical data still exist, record/flush failure, then follow the existing _Exit process-retention policy.
